name: Susannah Lamoreux

events.title: Marriage to David Prindle
events.description: Married in the afternoon by Rev. Silas Constant, who had spent the previous day at 'Mr. Davenport's'.

bioAdditions:
The journal of the Rev. Silas Constant, published in 1903, records that on 3 Sep 1783, after a day at 'Mr. Davenport's' in Smith's Clove, he 'married David Prindle and Susanna Lamoreux'. His marriage list for 1783 gives the same couple and date (S1). The editor's note identifies Susanna as a daughter of John Lamoreux Sr. of Smith's Clove, named in his will. That will (dated 31 Dec 1808 in one note, 1801 in another) names children Jane, Elizabeth, Charity, Martha, Phebe, Susanna, Hannah, Thomas, John, Robert, Joshua B. and Isaac. The editor also suggests David Prindle was 'probably of the Waterbury family of that name' (S1).

Giles & Franklin give her children as Elizabeth (m. Miles Davenport), Minerva (m. ___ Underwood) and Frances (m. Freeman Polk), and note that David was also called 'Pringle-Miller' (S2). Constant also married her sister Phebe to James Prendle on 19 May 1785 (S1).

conflicts.assessment: Constant's own journal entry and list give 3 Sep 1783. '22 July' is the date of the preceding entry in his list (Francis Gale and Elizabeth Lewis), so Giles & Franklin misread it.

conflicts.foundValue: The Lamoureux Record (1919) says Susanna married 'James Prindle' on 22 Jul 1783
conflicts.assessment: The 1919 statement is a misreading; Constant's journal plainly says David Prindle, and James Prendle married Phebe in 1785.

relationships.evidence: Constant's journal and marriage list, 3 Sep 1783

confidenceRecommendation.justification: Marriage recorded by the officiating minister in his contemporaneous journal; parentage from the editor's reading of John Lamoreux's Orange Co. will.
